papers.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
papers.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems
papers.abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation combines pre-trained parametric and non-parametric memory for language generation. The model retrieves documents from a dense vector index and conditions a sequence-to-sequence generator on retrieved passages. It is evaluated on knowledge-intensive NLP tasks including open-domain question answering.
findings: Combines a parametric seq2seq model with a non-parametric memory of retrieved text.
Uses retrieved passages from a dense vector index.
Reports improvements on several knowledge-intensive NLP tasks.
Does not claim that retrieval fully solves hallucination.
limitations: faithfulness is improved but not guaranteed

papers.title: REALM: Retrieval-Augmented Language Model Pre-Training
papers.venue: Proceedings of the 37th International Conference on Machine Learning
papers.abstract: REALM augments language model pre-training with a latent knowledge retriever. The model retrieves documents during pre-training and fine-tuning, and reports improvements on open-domain question answering benchmarks.
findings: Treats retrieved documents as latent variables.
Reports gains on open-domain QA tasks.
limitations: retrieval corpus and pre-training design shape results

papers.title: Dense Passage Retrieval for Open-Domain Question Answering
papers.venue: Proceedings of the 2020 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
papers.abstract: Dense Passage Retrieval uses a simple dual-encoder framework to retrieve passages for open-domain question answering. It shows that dense representations can outperform traditional sparse retrieval baselines in several QA settings.
findings: Uses separate encoders for questions and passages.
Provides a dense retrieval alternative to sparse lexical retrieval.

papers.title: Leveraging Passage Retrieval with Generative Models for Open Domain Question Answering
papers.abstract: Fusion-in-Decoder processes retrieved passages independently in the encoder and fuses evidence in the decoder for open-domain question answering. The work focuses on open-domain QA performance, not clinical safety standards.
findings: Introduces a passage fusion strategy for generative open-domain QA.
Evaluates retrieved passages with generative models.
Does not establish clinical safety standards.

papers.title: Precise Zero-Shot Dense Retrieval without Relevance Labels
papers.abstract: HyDE generates a hypothetical document for a query, encodes that document, and uses it for zero-shot dense retrieval without relevance labels. The evidence supports usefulness for zero-shot retrieval, but not universal elimination of labels in every retrieval domain.
findings: Uses hypothetical documents to support zero-shot dense retrieval.
Does not prove that labels are unnecessary in every domain.

papers.title: Large Language Models Encode Clinical Knowledge
papers.abstract: This paper evaluates large language models on clinical knowledge tasks. It is a clinical QA and medical LLM evaluation paper, not an in-scope retrieval-augmented architecture paper for open-domain QA.
findings: Clinical knowledge evaluation is outside the packet scope.
Not a core RAG architecture paper for open-domain QA.

papers.title: Attention Is All You Need
papers.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems
papers.abstract: Introduces the Transformer architecture. It is important background for modern NLP but does not study retrieval-augmented generation or open-domain QA retrieval architecture.
findings: Transformer background only; outside current retrieval-augmented QA scope.
